newsitem.title: USA: Ogden subsidiary offers to lease Iowa track.
newsitem.headline: Ogden subsidiary offers to lease Iowa track.

text.p: Ogden Entertainment Inc, a subsidiary of Ogden Corp, has proposed to lease, operate and add 400 slot machines to a profitable, publicly owned racetrack and casino near Des Moines, Iowa.

The Ogden proposal for the Prairie Meadows Race Track would seek to resolve issues surrounding the facility owned by Polk County and operated by the Racing Association of Central Iowa, a letter Friday from West Des Moines attorney Michael Sellers inviting negotiations states.

Iowa law bars Polk County from holding the operating license for the facility and in late July, the Iowa Racing and Gaming Commission began license revocation proceedings to determine if the association is the true operator of the facility.

Ogden's offer includes $30 million per year to Polk County on a five-year lease and $2 million per year, plus 10 percent of the earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization for the racing association.
Ogden would also have the option of extending the lease another five years and would pay Polk County supplemental income earmarked for capital development at the facility.
Polk County acted as underwriter for the Prairie Meadows bonds to keep the facility afloat and is now considering selling the facility.
The installation of slot machines in 1995 turned the track's fortunes around, allowing Polk County to retire the debt and project a profit for fiscal 1998.

The state racing and gaming commission is expected to authorize the license revocation hearing at a meeting later in August, administrator Jack Ketterer said. If so, the hearing would begin September 18, he said.
Sellers declined to comment on the letter to Ketterer, Racing Association Chairman James Rasmussen and Polk County Board Chairman Florence Buhr.
Ketterer noted that negotiations between Polk County and the racing association were incomplete and the Ogden offer is several steps away from needing state commission consideration.
